cultural.vision_reason: This hand-colored lithograph, from McKenney & Hall's Indian Gallery portraits, depicts Sequoyah, the Cherokee inventor of the syllabary, wearing traditional Cherokee dress (turban, layered garments, medal) and displaying his alphabet table — a documentary-type portrait recording actual Cherokee attire and cultural achievement, not an outsider caricature or a different people's material.

physical.title: book-illustration; print
physical.summary:
Print, illustration to Thomas L. McKenny and James Hall 'History of the Indian Tribes of North America with biographical sketches and anecdotes of the principal chiefs embellished with one hundred and twenty portraits, from the Indian gallery in the Department of War, at Washington" Philadelphia 1838 (vol.1 page 63 ); portrait of Sequoyah (SE-QUO-YAH) also known as George Guess, inventor of the Cherokee alphabet. He wears head-dress, several layers of garment and medal hanging on a ribbon around his neck; smoking a long thin pipe and holding a tablet with letters of the alphabet.
Lithograph, hand-coloured
